title: California's 26th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: California's 26th Congressional District, covering most of Ventura County and extending into northern Los Angeles County, is an open seat for the first time in more than a decade after incumbent Democrat Julia Brownley announced her retirement. The general election will feature Democrat Jacqui Irwin, a California State Assemblymember and former Thousand Oaks mayor, facing Republican Sam Gallucci, a pastor, nonprofit founder, and former business executive. Under California's top-two primary system, Irwin placed first and Gallucci second in the June 2 primary, advancing past seven other candidates. Cook Political Report rates the district as Solid Democratic, but the race reflects broader midterm dynamics including voter concerns over the cost of living, healthcare, immigration, and wildfire resilience.
polling_note: No independent general-election head-to-head polls were found for this race as of June 2026. Cook Political Report rates the district as 'Solid D' based on the Cook Partisan Voting Index (D+9) and historical voting patterns.

candidates.name: Jacqui Irwin
candidates.summary: Jacqui Irwin is a California State Assemblymember representing the 42nd Assembly District since 2014, and a former Thousand Oaks City Council member and two-term mayor. Before entering public service, she worked as an engineer at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Lab and Teledyne Systems, and holds a BS in Systems Engineering from UC San Diego, where she was an All-American swimmer. In the Assembly, she has chaired the Military and Veterans Affairs Committee and the Revenue and Taxation Committee, and currently chairs the Joint Committee on Climate Change Policies.

candidates.name: Sam Gallucci
candidates.summary: Sam Gallucci is a Republican candidate, pastor, nonprofit founder, and former business executive. He served as senior pastor at Embrace Church in Oxnard and founded The Kingdom Center, which provides emergency shelter and transitional housing for at-risk women and children, and Treasured Harvest, which supplies food and resources to farm workers. Earlier in his career, he worked at IBM and rose to Executive Vice President and General Manager at PeopleSoft. He holds an associate's degree from Grossmont College and a bachelor's degree from San Diego State University.

forecast.rationale: No independent general-election head-to-head polling exists for this race as of June 2026, so confidence is capped at medium and the forecast relies on structural and contextual indicators. Those indicators point strongly toward a Democratic hold: the district has a Cook PVI of D+9, Cook Political Report rates it 'Solid Democratic,' and it has been represented by a Democrat for more than a decade. In California's top-two primary (June 2, 2026), Democrat Jacqui Irwin—a sitting State Assemblymember and former Thousand Oaks mayor—finished first, advancing past seven other candidates. Republican Sam Gallucci, a pastor and former business executive with no elected office experience, placed second. While the open-seat dynamic and broader midterm concerns (cost of living, healthcare, immigration, wildfire resilience) introduce some uncertainty, the district's strong Democratic partisan baseline, Irwin's substantial local elected experience, and primary placement suggest an overwhelming Democratic advantage.
